item.title: cmd_checksums overwrites checksums.sha256 with empty file when all hash operations fail
item.intent: cmd_checksums must refuse to overwrite checksums.sha256 if the generated temp file is empty, and exit non-zero with a clear error.
item.description: In cmd_checksums(), the hash loop writes hashes to a temp file and then runs 'mv "$tmp" "$checksum_file"' unconditionally. If every hash_cmd invocation fails silently (e.g. file not found, hash binary returns non-zero), the temp file remains empty and the mv replaces the real checksums.sha256 with an empty file. All subsequent 'aishore update' runs will then fail integrity checks or accept a corrupt state.
steps: After the hash loop, check that the temp file is non-empty: [[ -s "$tmp" ]] || { log_error "No checksums generated — aborting to protect $checksum_file"; return 1; }
Run shellcheck — confirm zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: Running cmd_checksums when all files are missing exits non-zero and does not modify checksums.sha256
Normal run with valid files still writes checksums.sha256 as before
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
